Consult Summary:
- Female patient with 2 days of gradually worsening constant burning lower abdominal pain, associated with feeling hot/sweaty, mild nausea, and pink-tinged urine; empiric treatment for possible UTI started (Trimethoprim) and pregnancy test recommended.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Lower abdominal (just below the belly button) burning pain for ~2 days, gradual onset, constant and worsening.
  - Pain described as sore with pressure.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Feeling hot and sweaty.
  - Mild nausea; no vomiting.
  - Noted pink-colored urine; increased urinary frequency.
  - Prior constipation last week that has improved; current bowel movements normal; no diarrhea.
  - No dysuria/stinging on urination reported.
  - No measured fever (patient felt hot but did not check temperature).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no shortness of breath, no cough, no palpitations, no headaches, no visual changes.
  - No recent change in sexual partners.
- Past medical / surgical history and medications:
  - No surgical history.
  - No regular medications except Implanon contraceptive (inserted ~1 year ago).
- Sexual/reproductive history:
  - Sexually active with a single partner; last sexual activity ~4 days ago.
  - Last STD screen normal ~6 months ago.
  - Menstruating; patient stated last period "about three weeks ago. I mean, two weeks ago." (conflict noted).
  - Pregnancy is possible theoretically due to Implanon failure; clinician recommended pregnancy test.
- Social history / preventive care:
  - Lives in a shared house with two roommates.
  - Employed as an accountant.
  - Non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings:
  - Patient reports lower abdominal soreness/tenderness when she presses on the area (reported by patient; no clinician-measured exam findings documented).

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: probable urinary tract infection (provisional).
- Differential considerations discussed: gastrointestinal cause and pregnancy-related cause.

Plan:
- Assessment/diagnostic plan:
  - Clinician offered to arrange tests (implied urine testing) to help determine cause.
  - Patient preferred to start empiric treatment rather than await tests.
  - Pregnancy test advised to exclude pregnancy-related causes.
- Treatment and advice given:
  - Antibiotic prescribed: Trimethoprim. Transcript dose/frequency instructions inconsistent (see conflicts below). Patient instructed to collect prescription from pharmacy and start today.
  - Analgesia: Paracetamol advised for pain.
  - Supportive care: Drink plenty of fluids; cranberry juice suggested for urinary symptoms.
  - Safety-netting: Return or call if symptoms worsen or do not improve in a few days; warning signs include worsening abdominal pain, high/persistent fever, ongoing vomiting.
- Follow-up:
  - Patient advised to follow up if not improving or if symptoms worsen; clinician requested a follow-up contact in a few days if needed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Complete current medication list besides Implanon not documented.
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure) not recorded.
  - Formal physical examination by clinician not documented.
  - Results of any urine dipstick, urinalysis, urine culture, or pregnancy test not documented.
  - Documentation of whether a prescription was electronically sent (pharmacy details) beyond verbal agreement.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient name referred to as "Tim" by clinician and "Kim" elsewhere (conflict noted).
  - Timing of last menstrual period: initially "about three weeks ago" then corrected to "two weeks ago" (conflict noted).
  - Antibiotic dosing instructions inconsistent in transcript: clinician said both "two tablets" and "one tablet twice a day for three days" (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Adequate conversational transcript with some disfluency and repetition; no major inaudible segments noted.
